utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-42/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Kovacevic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was on the wrong channel. Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacevic. May I have the appearances. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For the Prosecution Susan L. Somers, senior trial attorney, Mr. Philip Weiner, co-counsel and Ms. Victoria McCreath, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radosavljevic. First of all, good afternoon to all of you both in and outside the courtroom. As announced on the 3rd of November during the Initial Appearance, the Chamber decided that we'll meet within the 30 days as we find them in the year, in the Rules, the 30 days in which, under normal circumstances, a plea would be entered. Since there might be a few medical issues to be discussed, I suggest to the parties that we'd go into private session in order to be able to freely discuss rather personal and medical matters. I see no objections. Therefore, Madam Registrar, I'd like to go in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now are in open session again, after having discussed mainly medical issues in private session. Ms. Radosavljevic, is there any other issue you'd like to raise now in open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not for the moment. Not for the Prosecution either. Then as far as the timing of the medical examination is concerned, I did understand that the assignment is about to take place and that one of the reasons why number 1 of the list was not chosen is availability, that's -- although, the difference in time -- the delay caused by that would not have been very substantial; but nevertheless, the -- it is preferred to have the report as soon as possible. I take it that it will take, to prepare the report, one or two weeks, but I have to ask you to get in touch with the Registrar, who's finally responsible for the assignment of these experts. The Chamber, however, wants to be informed on a regular basis, and the Chamber intends to have an appearance with regular intervals so that we don't lose track; that is to say, that at approximately every 30 days we would have an appearance, at least a court hearing, in which the Chamber is further informed about the progress made up till that moment. These hearings will be scheduled after consultation with counsel, in order not to create a situation where unnecessary travelling is needed to attend those hearings; and that's especially too for the -- for the Defence, I would say. If there's no further issue to be discussed at this moment, I announce that a decision on granting a further delay for entering a plea will be delivered on shortest notice; that means within a couple of days. And we now are adjourned.
